nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Short, dark winters and bright summers set the growing season for plants from the glens to the high plateaux.

nodes.name: Rain and cloud
nodes.desc: Moist, cool Highland weather keeps the moorland, bog and forest floor damp and supports mosses, heather and blaeberry.

nodes.name: Snow cover
nodes.desc: Long-lying snow patches persist on the high plateaux, shaping which plants and animals can live in the arctic-alpine zone.

nodes.name: Peaty acid soil
nodes.desc: Cool, wet ground builds acidic peat soils under much of the moorland and bog, favouring heather and cottongrass.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead pine needles, heather, and animal remains, returning nutrients to the peaty soil.

nodes.name: Scots pine
nodes.desc: The dominant native conifer of the Caledonian pinewood. Seedlings are often eaten by deer, which limits regrowth in many places.

nodes.name: Heather
nodes.desc: Dwarf shrub that blankets the moorland. A key winter food for mountain hares, and eaten by deer and grouse.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: Low shrub of the pinewood floor and moor; its leaves and berries feed deer, hares and capercaillie.

nodes.name: Rowan
nodes.desc: Small native tree of glens and woodland edges that bears berries and leaves taken by birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Crowberry
nodes.desc: Evergreen dwarf shrub of moor and mountain ground whose berries are eaten by grouse and capercaillie.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: Scotland's largest land mammal. Heavy grazing and browsing on heather, bilberry and young pines shapes how forest and moor regrow.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: Smaller deer of woodland edges that browses shrubs, heather and bilberry, and young trees.

nodes.name: Mountain hare
nodes.desc: Isolated Scottish population of the moors and hills; eats heather and, in snowy times, twigs and bark. A main prey of golden eagle and fox.

nodes.name: Western capercaillie
nodes.desc: Huge grouse of the old pinewoods, feeding on pine shoots and bilberry; its eggs, chicks and adults are taken by predators.

nodes.name: Willow ptarmigan
nodes.desc: Moorland gamebird that feeds mainly on heather shoots and also on crowberry and cowberry; prey for eagles and foxes.

nodes.name: Red squirrel
nodes.desc: Lives in pine woods, where it feeds on pine seeds and other tree fruits.

nodes.name: European pine marten
nodes.desc: Agile woodland hunter that takes squirrels, voles, birds and their eggs, as well as berries.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Generalist predator and scavenger; a major predator of mountain hares and a taker of grouse and carrion.

nodes.name: Scottish wildcat
nodes.desc: Rare forest-and-moor cat that hunts rabbits, hares, voles and birds.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: Small slender hunter of voles, rabbits, hares and ground-nesting bird eggs and chicks.

nodes.name: Carrion crow
nodes.desc: Opportunist that scavenges carcasses such as winter deer carrion and also takes eggs.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: Top predator of the open hills; takes hares and grouse and scavenges carrion in winter.
